The Irish bouzouki is an adaptation of the Greek bouzouki in Irish traditional music, a plucked instrument of the chordophone class, Hornbostel–Sachs 321.321. It commonly has four courses, mostly tuned G2-D3-A3-D4, a body that is mostly flat-backed with straight sides and a scale length of about 60 to 65 centimetres. The player provides chord or countermelody accompaniment by plucking, while the melody is usually taken by the flute, the fiddle and the like; it was introduced in the 1960s by Johnny Moynihan and others, then carried forward by Andy Irvine, Dónal Lunny and the maker Peter Abnett, and it is also found in the folk music of England, Scotland, Canada, the United States, Asturias, Galicia, Brittany and Scandinavia.
